checks: No eclipse at 1 of 52 covered epochs where the 1.96195 d period predicts one (each under half the typical depth, > 5 sigma below it). The period is probably wrong - the dips seen may be separate eclipses of a longer-period system.
writeup: TIC 340551910 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 1.9619 days. The system shows a primary eclipse with a depth of 3.05 percent dimming and a secondary eclipse detected at 5.9 sigma significance. Analysis of TESS photometry data yielded a strongべyon-Lomb-Scargle detection signal of 121.3, while pixel-level difference imaging confirmed the signal with a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 36.2, though the centroid offset measured 3.2 arcseconds from the target location. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel find. Machine learning screening assigned it a score of 0.69, indicating the automated pipeline considers it likely to be a genuine eclipsing binary. The data passed all quality checks without flags.
